_todo: Corrected a second time from the site owner's direct wiring description (the first correction had Port A bit 6=inverter-enable/bit 7=track-detect, and Port B as consecutive ranges 0-2 motors/3 spare/4-6 signal/7 status -- both wrong, discovered when firing 'motor bit 0' during Motor Scan lit a signal lamp instead of moving anything). Now correct: Port A bits 0-5 = switch feedback (in-pu), bit 6 = track detection input (in-pu), bit 7 = inverter-enable (starts 'in', becomes an output driven low by Firmware.ino's apply_board_hw() AFTER the normal safe-default writes -- not declared 'out' here on purpose, see PLAN_Phase3.md). Port B is NOT consecutive ranges: bits 0,2,4 = the 3 signal lamps, bits 1,3,5 = the 3 switch motors (interleaved with the signal bits, one motor/one signal alternating), bit 6 = status LED, bit 7 = spare motor driver output (wired but unused, no switch attached, no feedback either).

Signal lamp dimming is analog on the board now, not something firmware drives -- the old software-PWM digital fade (FadeGroup/ApplyNormalOutputsSlowly from SignalLys_2X_Momentbrytere.ino) is superseded and its EEPROM/wire-protocol support (fadeConfig) has been removed. Bits 0,2,4 here are still plain 'out' either way -- the fade method was never a hardware.json modeling question, just an operational one.

Board names use plain ASCII (Hoyre, not Høyre) on purpose, and match boards.json's naming ("Fossli Motors Hoyre"/"Fossli Motors Venstre") rather than the older FCSBR/FCSBL abbreviations -- this field is informational only (never consumed as a key, vaddr is), but kept consistent regardless.
